newsitem.title: USA: Albany Cty, N.Y. official to soon decide on bonds.
newsitem.headline: Albany Cty, N.Y. official to soon decide on bonds.

text.p: Albany County, N.Y.'s comptroller told the Albany Times Union that he does not expect to decide until Thursday on whether to approve the local airport's plans to sell $110 million of bonds.

However, the paper said Michael Conners proposed an alternative, selling the bonds in the competitive market instead of through a negotiated sale, a move that he said could save up to $500,000 in underwriting fees.
Further, a competitive sale does not require the county comtproller's approval, he told the paper.
While saying a competitive sale "is an option," John Egan, chief executive officer of the airport, said it had been rejected by 44 investment bankers who offered to broker the deal.
Egan said the bankers concluded a negotiated sale would be less costly in part because the authority was a first-time issuer, the Times Union reported.
Egan said that if Conners refused to approve the bond sale, which would be led by Lehman Brothers, the airport authority has other options, though he did not disclose them.
The authority had planned to sell the bonds on January 13, but Conners objected to the sale on Monday, saying a 20-year term would be less costly than the 30-year maturity the authority sought.
The sale of revenue bonds to finance a $158 million expansion had been unanimously approved by the Albany County Airport Authority.
